title: The play fails although a manual SSH test succeeds
scenario: The approved task collects show version and show ip interface brief from r1 only. A manual check works, but a new Ansible run fails. The following effective inventory was inspected without printing passwords. Both tests use the same Ubuntu account and verified target key.

exhibits.title: Working manual test
exhibits.text:
ssh labreader@10.42.0.2 succeeds.
Both approved show commands work at R1>.

exhibits.title: Run evidence
exhibits.text:
ansible_host: 10.42.0.2
ansible_user: retired-reader
Authentication failed; no stdout returned.
Approved change record: retired-reader removed; labreader remains the collection account.

question: Which correction is supported before rerunning the collection?
options: Increase the command timeout and leave the selected user unchanged.
Remove the interface command because any FAILED result proves login succeeded.
Use the approved labreader identity in the effective inventory.
Disable host-key checking because a password failure means the key changed.
explanation: The supposedly equivalent tests selected different usernames. Address, host identity and manual permissions were checked; the explicit authentication error occurs before command output. A timeout or command edit does not correct that account difference, and no host-key mismatch was observed.
fix: Change the applicable inventory variable to `ansible_user: labreader`; do not recreate the retired account. Verify the effective nonsecret settings and run `ansible-playbook -i inventory.yml collect.yml --limit r1 --list-hosts`. Then execute the same approved collection with `--limit r1 --ask-pass`, supplying the labreader password. Retain the returned version/interface output and compare it with the manual result. Keep host-key checking enabled and record that this repair changed the collection identity, not router configuration.

title: The report stops before showing the interface table
scenario: A one-router play collects operational output, then displays result.stdout_lines[1]. It uses normal error handling. Manual SSH from the same control user reaches the intended router, and the supported interface command works there.

exhibits.title: Collection task
exhibits.text:
cisco.ios.ios_command:
  commands:
    - show version
    - show ip interfaces brief
register: result

exhibits.title: Observed run
exhibits.text:
YAML syntax check passes.
Device parser rejects "show ip interfaces brief".
The second debug task is not executed.
Manual "show ip interface brief" returns the intended interface table.

question: Which repair addresses the evidence?
options: Change stdout_lines[1] to stdout_lines[0] and rerun the same command list.
Correct interfaces to interface in the collection task and rerun it.
Add ignore_errors so the following debug task can count as successful collection.
Replace the SSH password because the recap includes a failed task.
explanation: The device rejected a mistyped command. The unchanged index 1 correctly refers to the second command once that command succeeds. Ignoring a failure does not supply the expected result, and the device parser response does not indicate rejected authentication.
fix: In the fault copy, change only the line to `- show ip interface brief`. Run the syntax check, inspect `--limit r1 --list-hosts`, and execute the repaired file with the same limit and `--ask-pass`. Verify that the IOS command task succeeds and its following display contains the actual interface output from r1. Compare its address/state with the manual baseline. Preserve the failure record and note that show version may have executed before the bad second command.
